correctness.rationale: Exact offset interval geometry for arbitrary convex bases gives (b-a)+, 2min(a,b), (a-b)+, where a=width sqrt(1-c²), b=Hc. Their analytic sphere-coordinate integrals and Cauchy mean width yield a normalized three-state law. f_H(w)=w atan(H/w) has strictly negative second derivative -2H³/(H²+w²)². Strict Jensen proves equality iff constant width, Taylor integral remainder proves variance bounds, and a one-variable strictly decreasing stationary equation proves a unique global optimum. Independent normal/offset quadrature over four shape families and separate derivative tests passed.

value.rationale: The geometric observation of whether an invariant random affine plane cuts 0,1,2 basal faces is motivated by stereological microscopy of finite rods. The result extends the exact published law from circular bases to arbitrary nonsmooth convex bases, obtains an unexpected shape-invariant crossing-balance identity, identifies a sharp universal 64% best probability and complete constant-width equality class, and yields a quantitative deficit tied to width anisotropy. These are structural, sharp all-body results with clear calibration relevance, not a table update.
